title: Geometric points of an oriented product form a conservative family
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $f:T\to B$ be a morphism of schemes and let $V_f=T_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{B_{\mathrm{Et}}}B_{\mathrm{Et}}$ be the oriented product of the small etale topoi, with its triple site and projections as in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] and [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. For every geometric point $x$ of $T$, every geometric point $y$ of $B$, and every specialization $c$, a $2$-morphism from $y$ to $f(x)$, let $z_{x,y,c}:\mathbf{Set}\to V_f$ be the corresponding point of the oriented product. The inverse-image functors $z_{x,y,c}^*$ are jointly conservative on sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules and on their unbounded derived category: a morphism is an isomorphism if and only if all its pullbacks along these points are isomorphisms.

source.place: Exposé XI 1.8 (all points are triples), 2.5 and 2.7 (the oriented product site is coherent and pointwise testing is conservative); Stacks sites.tex Tag 00YQ (Proposition criterion-points).
